data.name: Jordan
data.summary: Jordan taxes income arising in or from Jordan. Capital gains made in Jordan are exempt (except on depreciable assets), Jordanian dividends are exempt, and foreign dividends are taxed only if they derive from money or deposits from inside Jordan. A foreign portfolio funded from abroad is therefore effectively untaxed. No wealth, inheritance or gift tax; property transfers cost about 6%. Top personal rate 30% (+1% national contribution above JOD 200,000) on taxable income. Corporate tax 20%.

regimes.name: Jordan tax residence
regimes.description: Source-based taxation: domestic gains and dividends exempt; foreign investment income taxed only if funded from Jordan.

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains generated within Jordan are exempt, except gains on depreciable assets (Income Tax Law No. 34 of 2014 as amended; PwC). Income is taxed only if it arises in or from Jordan; foreign-source investment income of a resident is taxable only where it derives from money or deposits from inside Jordan.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Foreign investment income derived from funds or deposits from inside Jordan is taxable (up to 30% + 1%).

open_questions: PwC states the 'money or deposits from inside Jordan' rule only for foreign dividends (and for companies' foreign investment income at 10%); whether foreign capital gains of an individual funded from Jordan are taxable was not verified. Once a family's money passes through Jordanian bank accounts, foreign income could become taxable at up to 30%.
capital_gains.rate_basis: All 0: domestic gains exempt by statute; foreign gains outside the source rule for a portfolio funded from abroad.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Gains on depreciable (business) assets are taxable; trading as a business not analysed.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Not taxed unless funded from inside Jordan (see above).

dividends.summary: Dividends from Jordanian resident companies are exempt. Dividends from non-residents are taxable only if they originate from money or deposits from inside Jordan (PwC).

dividends.rate_basis: Domestic 0 (exempt); foreign 0 for a portfolio funded from abroad. Headline 0.3 = top PIT rate that would apply to foreign dividends funded from Jordan (plus 1% national contribution above JOD 200,000).
dividends.withholding_outbound: No WHT on dividends paid by Jordanian companies (PwC).
dividends.treaty_network: More than 30 treaties (PwC); no treaty with the United States.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Annual municipal property (buildings and land) tax based on rental value, set locally. Property transfers are taxed at an aggregate rate of about 6%.

inheritance.summary: No inheritance, estate or gift tax; income from the distribution of estates or wills to heirs is exempt income (PwC).
inheritance.important_exceptions: Succession, not tax, is the issue: personal status law based on Sharia governs the estates of Muslims (fixed shares; a son typically takes twice a daughter's share; at most one third freely disposable by will to non-heirs). How estates of non-Muslim foreigners are handled (law of nationality, own religious rules, or Sharia by default) was not verified here; non-Muslim families should take local legal advice.

Succession of non-Muslims (church courts) versus Sharia rules not verified.

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident if actually residing in Jordan 183 days or more in the year (consecutive or not), or a Jordanian government employee abroad (PwC).

routes.name: Investor residence / citizenship by investment
routes.requirements: Jordan grants residence to property buyers and investors and has a citizenship-by-investment programme; thresholds not verified in this pass.

corporate.summary: CIT 20% plus 1% national contribution for most companies; 35% banks; 24% telecoms, insurance, financial intermediation, power and mining. Resident companies are not taxed on worldwide income except investment income from Jordanian funds (10%).
corporate.special_zones: Aqaba Special Economic Zone and development/free zones have reduced rates (not verified).

data.us_citizen_notes: US citizens remain US-taxed; no US-Jordan income tax treaty.

succession.name: Jordan
succession.summary: Muslim estates follow Sharia fixed shares, and a bequest cannot go beyond one third. Difference of religion bars inheritance (Personal Status Law 2019, art. 281/B). The sources found do not cover non-Muslim foreigners, trusts or foundations, so those answers are provisional.
succession.reserved_share: Muslims: Sharia fixed shares under the Personal Status Law 2019; religion is a bar to inheriting (art. 281/B); bequests are capped at one third of the estate (stated by Jordan's Iftaa Department, not the statute text).
succession.foreign_law_note: No source found on how Jordanian courts treat the estate of a non-Muslim foreigner or whether the national law applies. Christian communities have their own personal-status courts in Jordan (not sourced here).
succession.trust_note: No trust statute and no private-foundation law were found; Islamic waqf and charities exist but were not researched. Both answers are provisional, 'no' because nothing was found.
open_questions: Jordan's conflict rule for foreigners' estates (Civil Code) not found.
Whether Jordan has any trust or private-foundation law (and the status of family waqf) not found.
One-third cap is sourced to a fatwa, not the 2019 law.

Hague Trusts Convention: The HCCH status table (checked 2026-10-16) lists 14 Contracting Parties; this country is not one of them and no UK, Dutch or Chinese extension covers it, so the 1985 Convention is not in force here.
